title: Emit audit log events for Optimization Config lifecycle actions (create/validate/apply/promote/rollback) with SIEM-safe payloads
creator: Ethan Park
project: Safe apply + rollback mechanism (Cost Optimization Automation)
description:
Background
Enterprise prospects and existing Dedicated/Private customers are blocking on change-auditability for optimization tuning (batching/caching/quant profiles). We need a complete audit trail for Optimization Config changes that is suitable for SIEM export (Splunk/Sentinel/etc.) and meets our internal Security/Compliance requirements.

Scope
Emit structured audit log events for the full Optimization Config lifecycle:
- create_version
- validate_version (schema + semantic)
- apply_version (includes canary/staged rollout)
- promote_version (e.g., canary -> stable, staging -> prod pointer moves)
- rollback (revert to prior known-good)

Events must be emitted from the control plane service(s) that own the action, not the Console, and must include required metadata for traceability + forensics.

References / specs
- Confluence: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/optimization-config-audit-events.json
- Security working doc: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/security-and-compliance/audit-log-event-taxonomy-optimization.json
- Related PR implementation: sources/github/redwood/pr-19941-add-audit-log-events-for-config-changes.json

Requirements
1) Event taxonomy + naming
- Use the security-approved namespace and stable action verbs.
- Proposed canonical event names (final subject to Security sign-off):
  - optimization_config.version.created
  - optimization_config.version.validated
  - optimization_config.rollout.applied
  - optimization_config.rollout.promoted
  - optimization_config.rollout.rolled_back
- Ensure events are consistent across Hosted/Dedicated and Private control planes.

2) Required fields (SIEM-friendly)
All events MUST include:
- event_name
- event_time (RFC3339)
- actor_type (user | service | api_key)
- actor_id (user UUID or service principal)
- actor_email (if actor_type=user and available)
- request_id / trace_id (propagate from API gateway)
- ip_address (best-effort; may be absent for internal service calls)
- tenant_id
- environment (hosted | dedicated | private)
- scope (string-encoded; see below)
- config_id (stable logical ID)
- config_version_id (immutable version identifier)
- result (success | failure)
- error_code + error_message (when failure)

Rollout-specific required fields:
- rollout_id
- rollout_strategy (all_at_once | canary_percent | shard)
- canary_percent (if applicable)
- regions (comma-separated list)
- models (comma-separated list)
- previous_active_version_id (for promote/rollback/apply where pointer changes)
- new_active_version_id

Validation-specific required fields:
- validation_type (schema | semantic | both)
- validation_outcome (pass | fail)
- validation_errors (string; truncated/summarized; no nested arrays)

3) PII + secrets handling
- Do NOT log full config payloads (contains customer prompt-set identifiers in some Private setups; also too large).
- Include a safe diff summary:
  - changed_fields (comma-separated field paths)
  - risk_level (low | medium | high) based on semantic validation classification
  - diff_summary (human readable; max 2KB)
- No tokens, API keys, auth headers, or customer-provided prompt data.

4) Delivery + retention
- Events must go to the central audit pipeline used for enterprise exports.
- Ensure events have stable field names/types (string-only where possible).
- Ensure events are queryable by tenant_id, config_version_id, rollout_id, and request_id.

5) Coverage
- API-triggered actions (public/internal) must emit events.
- Console-triggered actions must emit via the same backend code path (no duplicate “UI-only” events).
- Background controller actions (rollout progression/pause) should emit events when state changes (applied->paused->failed->completed). If we decide not to emit pause/resume in v1, document explicitly.

Non-goals
- Not building the SIEM export UI; only producing correct structured events in the pipeline.
- Not guaranteeing exact-once delivery; we require at-least-once with idempotency keys to reduce duplicates.

Implementation plan
A) Define event schema + helpers
- Add an audit event builder in Optimization Config Service.
- Enforce a strict allowlist of fields; reject accidental payload additions.
- Provide helper to encode scope as a single string:
  - scope := "tenant=<id>;models=<m1|m2>;regions=<r1|r2>;mode=<hosted|dedicated|private>"

B) Hook emission points
- Create version endpoint: emit *.version.created
- Validate endpoint: emit *.version.validated (include errors summary on failure)
- Apply/rollout controller: emit *.rollout.applied at start; emit *.rollout.promoted when stable pointer changes
- Rollback endpoint: emit *.rollout.rolled_back (include from->to)

C) SIEM export compatibility
- Ensure all values are strings (even numeric percents) to avoid downstream schema drift.
- Keep payload < 8KB (Splunk HEC default safety); truncate diff_summary/validation_errors accordingly.
- Include event_id (UUID) + idempotency_key = "<event_name>:<request_id>:<config_version_id>:<rollout_id>".

D) Testing
- Unit tests for builder (field allowlist, truncation, actor derivation).
- Integration tests in apply/rollback flow verifying:
  - event emitted on success
  - event emitted on failure (result=failure + error_code)
  - request_id and tenant_id propagation
- Add a golden JSON snapshot test for each event type (string fields only).

Acceptance criteria
- For each lifecycle action (create/validate/apply/promote/rollback), an audit event is emitted exactly once per API request in the happy path.
- On failure paths, an audit event is emitted with result=failure and includes error_code/error_message (sanitized) and request_id.
- Events are visible in the audit pipeline with required tags (tenant_id, config_version_id, rollout_id) and can be joined to traces via request_id/trace_id.
- Security sign-off from Marcus Lin + Dr. Aisha Rahman on event taxonomy and payload fields.

Open questions
- Do we emit separate events for rollout pause/resume and gate failures (e.g., gate_failed) in v1? SRE prefers yes for forensics, but it increases volume.
- For Private deployments that may not have actor_email: do we include empty string vs omit field? Preference is include empty string for SIEM schema stability.

Notes
- Customer escalation history: missing rollback audit event noted in SUP-18544; this ticket must ensure rollback emits consistently and is covered by tests.
